<!-- pr-reviewer: e30244c56c3c3d4b83ba918259daffe3b3cffdc4 -->
No blocking findings. The PR is mergeable. The heavy result is still owed before merge.

This is a safety-tier review. The change affects generated contour depths.
The hull check covers each complete ring segment. Rings that fail this check retain the section checks.
Unreadable required sections now refuse a partial picked contour.
No goldens, UI files, dependencies, or process files change.

### Local build and tests

The first trial merge used main `fd64cc2f5ef78a76ae84d8447554f8adab144ed4`.
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran all 147 selected steps.
It passed 144 steps. Three multiaxis suites failed on the opening pose assertions.
I reproduced all three failures with the PR depth changes removed.

Upstream then merged the assertion repair in #3505.
I rebuilt the trial merge against main `835556814a9dc79ce7669320f402184b8ac7f8af`.
The trial merge is `8b91c41c1abd6ef2326377dec22473ea09b64613`.
Its first parent is this PR head.
The gate rerun with `--failed` passed all three failed suites.
I did not repeat the other 144 passed steps after this refresh.

- `multiaxis`: 7 passed.
- `multiaxis_avoid`: 6 passed.
- `multiaxis_rough`: 5 passed.
- Final `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- `git diff --check upstream/main`: PASS.

### Extra suites run

The fixture search found one consumer of `contour_outside_floor/fixtures/sign_plate_3443.json`.
I ran its complete suite again on the final trial merge:
`cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test contour_outside_floor`.
Both tests passed in 2.28 seconds. No tests were ignored.
No importer code or STEP fixture changes. The extra importer suites do not apply.

### Mutations

I compiled a temporary source copy with upstream's original `contour_depth.rs`.
A compiler wrapper selected that copy. The worktree source content did not change.

1. `picked_ring_refuses_unread_deeper_plane_after_clear_levels`: RED in debug. The original code returned a partial path.
2. `outside_sign_plate_reaches_bottom_with_four_tabs`: RED in release after 270.54 seconds. The path stopped at Z 7.061 and missed Z 6.

Both tests are GREEN with the fix on the final trial merge in debug.
No golden files moved, so there are no changed golden lines to inspect.

### Heavy lanes

The PR has priority P3. Current upstream AGENTS.md permits an owed heavy result for this priority.
`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` reaches all motion and app heavy targets.
Their status is **not run - owed to the wave run before merge**.
A green record must name this PR head before merge.

### Notes

`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_depth.rs` grows to 421 lines. This is a non-blocking file-size note.
The complete reported project was not run through the GUI, MCP, or the post flow during this review.
The regression checks the saved mesh through the motion generator.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Second read (read-only, not built) of head e30244c56c3c3d4b83ba918259daffe3b3cffdc4. This comment has no review marker. I did not change a label.

Verdict: no blocker.

## Gouge check
- The hull is the convex hull of each facet vertex. The XY projection of all material at each height is inside it.
- A ring is "clear" only when each vertex and each segment (the closing segment included) is outside the hull by `need + 1e-5`, with `need = r + leave - 0.008`. That is the slack of the old ladder. The cutter comes no nearer than before.
- A ring inside the hull, a ring that touches it, a concave part, an island and a part touch go to the section checks. That code did not change.
- NaN and values above 1e9 are refused before the arithmetic. There is no new `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` outside tests.

## Refusal
A picked ring with a section that cannot be read now refuses. Before, it got a part path and a note that was not true. That is the correct result by the Prime Directive. One case changes for the user: an inside picked ring on a mesh whose slice fails made a shallow path before, and refuses now.

## Notes, not blockers
- `bound` returns `Some` for an empty normalized region, and then each ring is "clear". The case needs a hull less than about 1e-6 mm wide. Filed as https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3517.
- Whole-model contours still write "the part is solid below it" when a section stopped the ring. Filed as https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3518, with the fixture size (1.29 MB).
- `contour_depth.rs` has 421 lines (406 on `main`). The file was over the limit before this PR.

## Not checked
I did not build. The heavy result is owed, as the review says. The trial merge with the current `main` and the covering heavy run are in the queue here.

Label: `merge-ready` removed until the owed heavy lanes are green on this head (e30244c). The clean review stands. The heavy run is in progress; when it is green, `merge-ready` goes back with the result recorded here.

Addressed: owed heavy lanes (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review", #3467).

Back to rework: this head breaks an app suite that its gate did not select.

`crates/app/tests/contour_whole_step.rs::whole_model_contour_that_cannot_reach_bottom_is_refused_with_the_stopped_level`

- Current `upstream/main` (`6e641dac7`): **passes**.
- `upstream/main` merged with this head (`e30244c56`): **fails**:

```
partial whole-model contour must not succeed cleanly; deepest=-0.5,
notes=Some(["Top below stock: the operation's top Z10.000 is below the stock top Z17.000 over its region - approach rapids may enter uncut stock; raise Top or face first"])
```

Found by the merge train (main + #3157 + #3160 + #3487) and confirmed alone on a trial merge. The new hull check lets a whole-model contour that the test says cannot reach the bottom succeed cleanly. Either the hull check must not apply here (the model's own footprint is not clear of this ring), or the test's premise changed - decide which and say why. The quick gate should also select `contour_whole_step` for `contour_depth.rs` / `contour_exterior.rs` changes; if the gate map misses it, note that for a follow-up.
